No, but it will significantly reshape the job landscape.

The pattern from previous technological shifts suggests that AI will eliminate some jobs, transform many more, and create new ones we haven't fully imagined yet. Jobs involving routine cognitive tasks are most vulnerable - think data entry, basic customer service, some junior analytical work. 

But jobs requiring physical dexterity in unstructured environments, complex human interaction, creative judgment, or dealing with novel situations are much harder to automate. A plumber navigating a weird old building, a manager handling interpersonal conflict, a researcher tackling truly new problems - these involve the kind of messy, context-dependent work AI struggles with.

The bigger question isn't really "will all jobs disappear?" but "how quickly will the transformation happen, and will our institutions adapt fast enough to help people transition?" That's where the real uncertainty and concern lives.

What's prompting your question - are you thinking about this for your own career, or more generally curious about the economic future?
